clue.text: Make stronger complaint against university parking

parts.note: a beef is a grumble or grievance
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Someone lodges a stiffer grievance against a university's parking rules.
explanation.definitionFit: To beef something up is an idiom for reinforcing or strengthening it.

clue.text: This writer set up device for exercise

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: the setter referring to themself, giving ME
a ploy is a stratagem or device

explanation.surface: The writer assembles a gadget for a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercise' looks like a noun, a workout, but it is the verb meaning put to use; 'set up' signals the turnaround in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise a skill or right is to use it, which is the verb's sense here.

clue.text: Contraband for bishop concealed without opening

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: the word for concealed loses its first letter, its opening

parts.note: concealed means hidden

explanation.surface: Smuggled goods were tucked away for a bishop in a hidden spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without opening' drops the H of HIDDEN, leaving IDDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Contraband goods are those whose import or possession is prohibited by law.

clue.text: Established source of company's aluminium in French region

parts.note: established, as a fact, means proven

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A firm's proven supply of aluminium is located in a region of France.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes something from or belonging to Provence, a region of southern France.

clue.text: Standing up against erroneous article

parts.note: v, for versus, means against

indicators.note: erroneous means wrong, so the letters are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone is taking a stand against a mistaken newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erroneous' rearranges ARTICLE into ERTICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something upright, perpendicular to the ground, is standing up.

clue.text: Vicars prepared to acquire English organs

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in another letter, acquiring it
prepared in the cookery sense of worked over, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Clergymen get ready to obtain some English church organs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges VICARS into VISCRA, which acquires E to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The viscera are the internal organs of the body, such as heart, liver and intestines.

clue.text: Field, originally orchard, lacking in fruit

indicators.note: the fruit is missing the letter picked out

parts.note: an orange is a fruit

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A field that was once an orchard now has no fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' picks the O of orchard; 'lacking in' takes it from ORANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a field or scope, as in the range of someone's interests.

clue.text: Up in arms, rodent in unrestricted view

indicators.note: the rodent sits inside the other letters
with its restricting outer letters removed, the word keeps only its centre

parts.note: a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: People protest angrily on seeing a rodent in plain sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unrestricted' looks like it means open or full, but here it removes the limits, the outer letters, of the word that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up in arms is an idiom for being angry and protesting.

clue.text: Notifying beer society about consignment at the back

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

indicators.note: the word for society goes around the letter picked out

parts.note: a ring is a group or cartel of people acting together

indicators.note: at the back points to the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A beer society is told about the end of a delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the back' picks T from consignment, and RING goes 'about' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Notifying someone is warning or informing them, as alerting does.

clue.text: Mock London club riven by sign of debt

indicators.note: riven means split, so the club's name is split open by the other letters

parts.note: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club
an IOU is a note acknowledging a debt

explanation.surface: A London club is torn apart by a sign that it owes money.
explanation.walkthrough: SPURS is Tottenham Hotspur, a north London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A mock item is fake or counterfeit, which is what spurious describes.

clue.text: Groom and knight dined

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight
having dined, one has eaten

explanation.surface: A bridegroom and a knight have had their dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: To groom is to tidy or smarten, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Phone not fixed

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a portable telephone and also describes anything able to move freely.

clue.text: Division line drawn in the ground

indicators.note: the other letters are placed inside the rearranged ones
ground as the past of grind, so the letters are crushed into a new order

parts.note: a drawn game ends level, even

explanation.surface: A boundary line is marked out on the earth to split it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' rearranges THE into ETH, and 'in' puts LEVEN inside.
explanation.definitionFit: One of eleven equal parts of a whole is a fraction, a division of it.

clue.text: Announcements not clear, said in garbled way

indicators.note: garbled means jumbled, so the words are said in a scrambled order

explanation.surface: Statements came out muddled, spoken in a confused manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal announcements or statements are declarations.

clue.text: Unrest when a foreign soldier replaces leader in headquarters

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is swapped out for other letters

parts.note: a station is a base, such as a police or military headquarters
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Trouble breaks out when an overseas soldier takes the top job at base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaces leader in' swaps the S of STATION for A GI.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitation is public disturbance or stirring up, a synonym of unrest.

clue.text: Eating popular bread covered with scrambled eggs

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: the bread is wrapped in the other letters
scrambled means jumbled, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: a tin is a loaf baked in a tin, a British bread

explanation.surface: A trendy breakfast: bread topped with scrambled eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: A tin, or tin loaf, is a British bread baked in a rectangular tin. 'covered with' has the anagram of the eggs wrapped round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingesting is taking food into the body, a formal synonym for eating.

clue.text: Driver in second and first tackling hill

indicators.note: the two time words take on the hill, holding it between them

parts.note: a mo is a short moment, a second
1st, written with I for one, is first
a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A driver changes from second to first gear to climb a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as gear changes; a tor is a rocky hill in south-west England, and 'tackling' sets it between the two time words.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorist is a person who drives a car.

clue.text: Sunbathing outside private place, municipal organisation

indicators.note: the sunbathing word goes around the other letters

parts.note: sunbathing to darken the skin is tanning
something private is one's own
Pl is the abbreviation for place in addresses

explanation.surface: Sunbathing outside one's own property is a matter for the local council.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts TANNING around OWNPL, after its T.
explanation.definitionFit: The planning of a city's layout and development is organisation at municipal level.

clue.text: Worried travelling over in North America

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the abbreviations

parts.note: US for United States, America

indicators.note: travelling suggests moving about, so the letters move

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious about travelling across North America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges OVER into ERVO, placed 'in' N and US.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nervous is feeling anxious or worried.

clue.text: Look out for period with internet being up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: an era is a period of time
the web is the internet

explanation.surface: A warning to watch out for the time when the internet is running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being up' turns ERAWEB backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Beware is a warning to be cautious of something, to watch for it.

clue.text: One accepting basic, once derelict, houses

indicators.note: the run of words contains the answer within it, as a house holds its occupants

explanation.surface: Someone settles for plain, once rundown homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' looks like a noun after 'derelict' but is the verb, holding the answer inside 'basiC ONCE DERelict'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who concedes admits or accepts a point or defeat.

clue.text: Buckle from pressure after endless conflict

indicators.note: the pressure letter comes after the trimmed word
the word for conflict loses its final letter

parts.note: a clash is a conflict
P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: A buckle gives way under pressure after an unending fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buckle' tempts as a verb, give way, but it is the noun, a fastening; 'endless' trims the conflict word and 'after' places the pressure letter last.
explanation.definitionFit: A clasp is a fastening device, of which a buckle is one kind.

clue.text: Criminal goaded, removing article for ruse

indicators.note: criminal means wrong, so the letters are put in a wrong order
one letter is taken from the pool before it is rearranged

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A goaded criminal discards an item in a trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges GOADED, and 'removing' takes away A, leaving the answer's five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a clever trick or scheme, a ruse.

clue.text: Return gutted after receiving bad news

indicators.note: the outer letters take the other letters in
a gutted word has its insides removed, keeping only its outside letters
bad suggests the letters are spoiled, put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone comes back devastated after hearing bad news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' looks like devastated in the surface but empties the word after it; 'receiving' wraps those outer letters round the anagram that 'bad' makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A return can mean a reply or response, as in a return of serve.

clue.text: Coarse kid, lad with heart in wrong place

parts.note: to kid is to tease, which is to rib

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word is moved to another position

explanation.surface: A rough boy, a lad with misplaced feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with heart in wrong place' moves the A of LAD to the front, giving ALD.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribald humour is vulgar and coarse.

clue.text: Regularly ignoring worrying sign, fault master

indicators.note: every other letter of the three words is skipped at regular intervals, the rest kept

explanation.surface: Constantly overlooking an alarming symptom is a failing of the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly ignoring' skips the first, third and every other odd letter of 'worrying sign fault', keeping the even ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A master is the first version from which copies are made, the original.

clue.text: Order rep's last stationery items

indicators.note: to order is to arrange, so the letters are put in a new sequence

explanation.surface: A sales rep's latest order of office supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a request to buy, but it means arrange the letters of REP'S LAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Staplers are desk devices for fastening paper, items of office stationery.

clue.text: Turning arm, see lump

indicators.note: turning means the word is turned around and read backwards

parts.note: a gun is a firearm, an arm
to see a point is to get it, understand

explanation.surface: Swivelling a limb, notice a swelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' reverses GUN to NUG.
explanation.definitionFit: A nugget is a small lump, especially of gold.
